'''''Trifolium resupinatum''''' ('''reversed clover''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=TRRE4|taxon=Trifolium resupinatum|accessdate=15 December 2015}}</ref><ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 }}</ref> '''Persian clover''', '''shaftal''', syn. ''T. resupinatum'' L. var. ''majus'' Boss., ''T. suaveolens'' Willd.) is an annual clover used as fodder and hay, which reaches {{convert|60|cm|in|abbr=on}} tall when cultivated, and forms rosettes when grazed or mowed.

It is native to central and southern Europe, the Mediterranean, and southwest Asia as far south as the [[Punjab region|Punjab]]. It is an important hay crop in cold regions of Iran, Afghanistan and other Asian areas with cold winters.
